reviewerOrPass: Worker A, same AI, separate source-first pass
method: Reconstructed the credit-bearing curriculum from the adopted Dutch-track table and the dated OSIRIS groups, rechecked entry and assessment against the individual course sheets, then reconsidered the two workbook schedules and the exact frozen audience record. The same AI performed this separate pass.
findings: Article 2 of Appendix I identifies the Dutch full-time track, some English-language units and 18 EC of free choice, distinct from the English track’s 30 EC. Distinct courses sum to 60 EC in each year. The repeated block appearances of Human Resource Studies and Organization Studies are 3+3 EC each, and the organisation project and thesis are 6+6 EC each. The 18 EC electives can combine minor and individual elective coursework. GROW entries are all zero credit.

The OER sets 42 first-year credits for positive binding study advice. The first-semester project uses team research with qualitative and quantitative components and required working groups. The separate spring thesis requires at least 120 EC within the programme, which the proposed route earns after the first two years. The course specifies individual work in supervised thesis groups, AI literacy modules and test, and a defence. No early-start exception is needed.

The closest UCR option covers organisational psychology, leadership, negotiation, public decisions and multiple empirical methods. The other option sustains product design, customer inquiry and responsible strategy with a technically grounded circularity strand. Feasibility is established by the current workbook. Course matches do not make UCR equivalent to Tilburg’s labour-law, organisation-network, consultancy and required research sequence. Both compulsory research units remain unpaired, with optional UCR research additional.

Read both concepts and schedules, all 35 selected course titles and descriptions, all 29 external component titles, five note anchors, both comparison notes, selected source links, programme title and normal-mode fallback. The English title is the review-index value as well as the canonical title. Internal evidence distinctions and source investigation do not become audience prose.
